Celebrating the molecule that changed the world
Source: © Shutterstock
First isolated by Michael Faraday 200 years ago, benzene’s properties have been exploited across many different fields
In 1825, Michael Faraday discovered one of the most fascinating compounds in chemistry:
benzene
. While isolating the components of oily residues of illuminating gas, Faraday identified a mysterious liquid, with a peculiar aromatic smell, which would go on to transform the landscape of chemistry.
Within the pages of the
Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London
, Faraday
described
this seemingly simple yet profoundly unique molecule. What set benzene apart, even in its earliest discovery, was its resistance to easy chemical classification. Its peculiar behaviour, such as its surprising stability despite being highly unsaturated, hinted at a deeper mystery that would not be fully resolved until the mid-19th century with the proposal of its cyclic structure.
Benzene’s physical properties only added to its mystique. This colourless liquid emitted a faintly sweet, intoxicating aroma – a hallmark of aromatic compounds. With a boiling point of 80.1°C, it was volatile and highly flammable, making it both a chemical curiosity and a potential industrial tool. Early chemists were captivated by its ability to dissolve fats, oils and other nonpolar substances, which made it a valuable solvent for experimentation and industrial processes. Yet, it was benzene’s chemical properties – its reactivity and stability – that would become the cornerstone of an entire branch of organic chemistry: aromatic compounds.
Today, benzene is everywhere, interwoven into the structures of more complex molecules that enhance our daily lives in fields as diverse as health, energy, advanced materials, electronics, food, dyes and biotechnology. This humble molecule opened the doors to a vast universe of aromatic compounds and an endless array of applications that have redefined our world.
Stability and tunability
Following benzene’s legacy came polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), a fascinating class of organic molecules composed of fused benzene rings. These structures not only preserve benzene’s aromatic stability, thanks to their electron delocalisation, but also exhibit unique electronic and optical properties determined by their size and arrangement. While smaller PAHs, like
naphthalene
and anthracene, had been characterised in the 19th century, the discovery of larger, more complex systems unveiled entirely new and surprising properties – from discrete energy levels in simpler molecules to semiconducting behaviours in larger systems like pentacene.
The synthesis and study of these compounds paved the way for nanographenes, opening new dimensions in chemistry and materials science. Through meticulous control over their molecular structures, researchers have learned to design advanced materials with tunable properties, such as electron conductivity, fluorescence, chirality and chemical reactivity. This painstaking precision highlights the intrinsic beauty of chemistry at its most fundamental level, an art of exactitude that continues to push the boundaries of possibility.
A landmark achievement in this journey was the discovery of hexabenzocoronene (HBC), in 1958. This molecule, composed of 42 carbon atoms forming 13 hexagonal rings in a perfectly flat structure, remained the largest fully characterised polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon for decades. Yet the creativity of organic chemistry knows no bounds. Klaus Müllen, a pioneer in the exploration of nanographenes, succeeded in 2002 in synthesising a remarkable structure formed by 222 carbon atoms with a diameter of 3nm, demonstrating the immense potential of organic synthesis to construct tailor-made graphene molecules.
Graphene stands out as the ultimate expression of benzene’s versatility
The fusion of benzene rings has given rise to some of the most remarkable materials in modern science, including fullerenes and carbon nanotubes. Fullerenes, often referred to as
buckyballs
, are spherical molecules composed entirely of carbon atoms arranged in a pattern of hexagons and pentagons, resembling a molecular soccer ball. These structures, discovered in 1985, owe their stability and symmetry to the aromaticity derived from benzene-like rings. Similarly, carbon nanotubes – long, cylindrical structures composed of fused aromatic rings – have captivated scientists with their extraordinary strength, flexibility and electrical conductivity. Both fullerenes and nanotubes exemplify the limitless potential of carbon chemistry, with benzene as the foundational building block.
Among these innovations, graphene stands out as the ultimate expression of benzene’s versatility. This two-dimensional material, consisting of a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb lattice,
44290413.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了苯分子在化学史上的重要性及其广泛应用。苯由迈克尔·法拉第于1825年首次分离出来，其独特的稳定性与化学性质使其成为有机化学中芳香族化合物的基石。苯的特性使其在溶解非极性物质方面具有重要价值，并且它的发现启发了多环芳烃（PAHs）等化合物的发展。这些化合物具有独特的电子和光学特性，推动了纳米石墨烯等先进材料的研发，广泛应用于健康、能源、电子等领域。此外，苯的环状结构也是富勒烯和碳纳米管的基础，这些材料展现出极高的强度和导电性。文章特别提到，石墨烯作为苯分子多样性的终极体现，是当前科学研究的前沿材料之一，展示了有机化学在材料科学中的无限潜力。

data.title: Darklang Goes Open Source
data.author: stachudotnet
data.article_summary: Dark Inc. 已关闭并成立 Darklang Inc.，同时将所有代码库开源，采用 Apache License 2.0。最初，Darklang 作为一个托管平台，仅在 darklang.com 上编码并即时上线，以实现安全代码迁移和统一部署。然而，这种模式面临可持续性问题，且用户反馈显示产品成熟度才是采用障碍，而非许可证问题。随着技术方向转向本地开发，以及开发者工具市场成熟，公司决定开源以增强平台的可访问性和社区拥有感。开源还确保平台能够长期存在并发展，同时公司将通过团队协作和 AI 工具等收费服务获利。目前，仍在探索开源生态中的许可技术问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Darklang的语言设计、发展方向、商业模式及其与现有工具的比较

不同观点：
• **投资与公司关闭**：[simonw]提到Darklang公司在没有吸引到新投资的情况下关闭，并将产品出售给员工继续维护。这种做法被认为是一种有趣且不常见的模式，特别是在公司经营多年但缺乏市场牵引力的情况下。

• **核心用例不明**：[kburman]对Darklang的核心用例感到困惑，不确定它相较于Python或其他后端技术栈解决了哪些实际问题，并质疑团队在没有收入的情况下如何支撑两年的开发工作。

• **产品设计与取舍**：[sisve]认为Darklang在某些方面过于超前，选择了错误的路径，尤其是在对本地部署和数据主权支持上的不足。此外，对编辑器与语言的紧密耦合表示赞赏，但对产品转向表示失望。

• **开源与本地运行**：[freedomben]对Darklang从“源码可用”转向Apache 2许可表示赞同，并认为允许本地运行是一个正确的进展方向。

• **与其他语言的比较**：[jitl]提到Epic的Verse语言在处理可变变量上的独特方式，并暗示这种方法与Darklang的设计有相似之处。

• **结构编辑器的价值**：[notarobot123]对Darklang放弃结构编辑器表示失望，认为这是其核心价值之一，并对该决定背后的原因提出疑问。

• **语言实现与开源潜力**：[thesurlydev]对Darklang转向F#实现表示好奇，并期待开源后是否会有其他语言的移植版本。

• **LLM与编程环境**：[apgwoz]认为Darklang的基础设施非常适合LLM驱动的编程环境，并指出其目标是抽象复杂的部分，但现实中这些复杂部分可能是项目成功的关键。

• **文档与用户体验**：[tnolet]指出Darklang的文档和网站设计不够专业，认为良好的文档和用户体验设计将大大提高其采用率。

• **与Unison的比较**：[solomonb]提出Darklang与Unison语言的比较，希望了解两者的优劣。

• **对产品价值的质疑**：[mountainriver]直接质疑Darklang相较于Python等成熟语言的价值，要求更明确的解释。

补充讨论：
• **时间线与发展历程**：[cmontella]详细回顾了Darklang的发展历程，包括融资、团队缩减、产品重写和AI转向，并指出编程语言开发的难度和资金需求。

争议焦点：
• **核心价值与市场定位不清**：部分评论者对Darklang的市场定位和核心用例感到困惑，质疑其相对于现有工具的优势。
• **产品设计方向的转变**：对Darklang放弃结构编辑器和转向本地运行的决定存在不同看法，部分用户对此表示失望。
• **资金与可持续发展**：对编程语言开发的资金需求和商业模式存在争议，部分评论者认为传统的VC融资模式不适合此类项目。

总结：Darklang的讨论围绕其产品设计、市场定位、开源策略及与现有工具的比较展开，争议主要集中在核心价值不明确和产品设计方向的转变上。

44290653.article_content:
As part of
shutting down Dark Inc.
and
forming Darklang Inc.
,
we've finally open-sourced all of our repositories.
Our source code
is now under the Apache License 2.0.
For years, we wrestled with questions of sustainability and how to build something that truly empowers developers. We've long believed in open source philosophically, but felt that Darklang's unique architecture and business model required a different approach.
Why We Initially Chose Source-Available
We originally designed Darklang as a hosted-only platform where you'd code at darklang.com and programs would instantly be live in production. We believed this centralized approach was necessary for features like safe code migration and unified deployment, and that offering self-hosting would undermine our sustainability model.
The core challenge was building something valuable while ensuring we could continue working on it long-term. Traditional open source funding models all had limitations, so Darklang was designed as "a language with a business model" - users with serious workloads would fund ecosystem development through our hosting platform.
What Changed Our Thinking
Three key shifts changed our perspective:
Product maturity and user feedback
: The real barrier to Darklang's adoption was never licensing - it was product maturity. As we've gotten closer to building something people love, staying source-available started feeling like an unnecessary risk. We consistently heard that people wanted us to be more open.
Building for local-first development
: Our technical direction evolved significantly. We're now building Darklang to run locally as a CLI, with the ability to deploy to our cloud or elsewhere. Nobody wants to run a proprietary language binary on their own machine.
New business opportunities
: The developer tools market has matured since 2017. We now see successful companies charging for team collaboration features and AI-powered tools while keeping the core platform accessible. These create value that teams are willing to pay for, while always having the option to self-host.
Why Open Source
Open source enables Darklang to be accessible, inspectable, and community-owned. It aligns with our philosophy of democratizing programming and ensures the platform can persist and evolve regardless of any single company's fate.
We've learned how to deliver Darklang's key benefits - invisible infrastructure, deployless deployment, trace-driven development - without requiring our specific editor or hosting environment. This makes open source viable while preserving what makes Darklang special.
Open Questions
We're still exploring some interesting technical challenges around licensing in the Darklang ecosystem. GitHub handles this by attaching LICENSE.md files, but in a world where a package manager syncs types and functions directly, there are some neat challenges to think through. The core platform being open source gives us a solid foundation to build on.

data.title: Adding public transport data to Transitous
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Transitous是一个基于MOTIS引擎的公共交通路线服务，依赖全球数据来提供功能。用户可以帮助查找、添加和改善数据，类似于OpenStreetMap的社区贡献模式。要帮助改进，首先需对比Transitous数据与实际情况，检查交通时刻表是否准确及全面。若发现数据缺失或过时，可通过多种途径寻找GTFS数据，包括公交公司、开放数据门户和GTFS注册表等。添加GTFS数据通常只需在JSON文件中添加几行代码指向数据源。对于实时数据，GTFS Realtime（RT） feeds包括 trip updates、service alerts和vehicle positions，需与静态数据结合使用。通过命令行工具可以查看GTFS-RT内容。目前，Transitous覆盖55个国家，并持续更新。

which define all the datasets to be used as well as a few parameters and metadata for those.
Once a day those are then retrieved, validated, filtered and post-processed for importing into
MOTIS by
Transitousâ import pipeline
.
Public transport schedules
The backbone of public transport routing is static
GTFS
schedule data,
thatâs the bare minimum for Transitous to work in a region.
GTFS feeds are essentially zip files containing a set of CSV tables, making them relatively
easy to inspect, although especially nationwide aggregated feeds can get rather large.
GTFS feeds ideally contain data for several months into the future, but can nevertheless receive
regular updates. Transitous checks for updates daily, so for this to work practically we also need
a stable URL for them (that might seem obvious to you, but apparently not to all feed providersâ¦).
We currently have more than 1800 of those,
from 55 countries. The
Transitous map view
gives you an impression how well an area is covered,
each of the colored markers there is an (estimated) current position of a public transport vehicle.
Recently added coverage in South Korea.
If your area is incomplete or not covered at all, the hardest part to change that is probably finding
the corresponding GTFS feeds. Thereâs a few places worth looking at:
The public transport operators themselves, they might just publish data on their website.
Regional or national open data portals, especially in countries with regulation requiring public transport data to be published.
In the EU, those are called âNational Access Pointâ (NAP).
GTFS feed registries such as
Mobility Database
and
Transitland
.
Google Maps having public transport data in your region is a strong indicator whether GTFS feeds even exist,
as they use those as well.
Adding a GTFS feed to Transitous is then usually just a matter of
a few lines of JSON
pointing
to the feed. In rare cases it might require a bit more automation work, such as in France where thereâs
hundreds of small feeds to manage.
And every feed is welcome, no matter whether itâs a nation-wide railway operator or a single community-run bus
to help people in a rural area, as long as itâs for a service open to the general public.
Realtime data
So far this is all static though. For properly dealing with delay, disruptions and all kinds of other unplanned
and short-notice service changes we also need
GTFS Realtime (RT)
feeds.
Those are polled once a minute for updates.
GTFS-RT feeds come in three different flavors:
Trip updates, that is realtime schedule changes like delays, cancellations, etc.
Service alerts, that is textual descriptions of disruptions beyond a specific connection, such as upcoming construction work.
Vehicle positions, that is geographic coordinates of the current position of trains or busses.
MOTIS can handle the first two so far. Support for vehicle positions is also on the wishlist, and not just
for showing current positions on a map, vehicle positions could also be used to interpolate trip updates
when those are not available.
Adding GTFS-RT feeds to Transitous is very similar to adding static GTFS feeds, however GTFS-RT feeds usually only work
in combination with their respective static equivalent.
Combining a smaller realtime feed of a single operator with a nationwide aggregated static feed will thus usually
not work out of the box. Thereâs ways to exclude certain operators from a larger static feed though, so with a bit
of puzzle work this can usually be made to work as well.
GTFS-RT feeds use
Protocol Buffers
, but thereâs nevertheless simple way to look at their content:
curl https://the.feed.url | protoc gtfs-realtime.proto
--decode
=
transit_realtime.FeedMessage | less
The Protocol Buffers schema file needed for this can be downloaded
here
.

data.title: Quantum mechanics provide truly random numbers on demand
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）利用量子力学原理开发的真正随机数生成器。传统算法只能生成伪随机数，而量子力学由于其内在的随机性，可以生成无法预测的真正随机数。NIST通过贝尔测试实验，利用纠缠光子的特性，确保了随机数的真实性和可验证性。他们与科罗拉多大学博尔德分校合作，创建了“科罗拉多大学随机信标”（CURBy），每日自动生成并发布随机数，供公众使用。这是首个利用量子非定域性生成随机数的服务，具有高度透明性和可验证性，是随机数生成技术的一大里程碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：随机性的本质及其应用，特别是在量子物理和加密学中的角色。

不同观点：
• btilly认为https://www.random.org/提供的随机数足以满足任何需要，尤其是在需要公开验证的随机数场合。但同时指出，在加密学中，公开可验证性并不是理想特性。
• perching_aix质疑我们如何辨别“本体随机性”，并区分“认识论随机性”（即由于知识不足而显得随机）和“本体随机性”（即真正的随机性）。
• ang_cire对量子力学中波函数坍缩是否真正随机提出疑问，认为可能存在未知的变量影响测量结果。同时指出，经典例子如抛硬币，在完全掌握变量情况下是确定性的。
• t_mann讨论了在安全相关应用中使用公开随机数可能带来的风险，并提出通过哈希函数与秘密信息结合生成私有随机数的可能性。
• EastLondonCoder分享了一个关于硬件随机数生成器因过热而失效的真实案例，强调了在某些场景下使用物理随机数生成器的重要性。
• JKCalhoun提出将大量随机值写入硬盘以创建一次性密码本的想法，并认为这可能是最难破解的加密方式。
• gregfjohnson定义“随机”为是否存在一个能够预测下一个数值的算法，并提到了NIST量子信标作为例子。
• lacoolj持决定论观点，认为只要有足够的数据，宇宙中的任何事物都可以被预测，因此不存在“真正的随机”。
• oneshtein简短提到量子世界的数学模型可以提供真正的随机数。
• jmyeet深入探讨了“随机”这一概念的复杂性，并引用了Kolmogorov复杂性来解释随机性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了随机数生成器在实际应用中的故障案例（EastLondonCoder），以及如何将公开随机数安全地转化为私有随机数的讨论（t_mann）。
• 争议的焦点在于“真正的随机性”是否存在，以及量子力学中的随机性是否仅仅是由于未被完全理解的变量所导致的（ang_cire, lacoolj）。
• 评论中也提到了Kolmogorov复杂性作为衡量随机性的一个工具（jmyeet），并讨论了随机数生成器在加密学中的应用风险。

这些观点共同构建了对随机性本质及其应用的多元化理解。

The GIST
Quantum mechanics provide truly random numbers on demand
by
National Institute of Standards and Technology
edited by
Sadie Harley
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication
trusted source
proofread
Instrumentation for the quantum random number generator in the NIST Boulder laboratories. Credit: NIST
Randomness is incredibly useful. People often draw straws, throw dice or flip coins to make fair choices. Random numbers can enable auditors to make completely unbiased selections. Randomness is also key in security; if a password or code is an unguessable string of numbers, it's harder to crack. Many of our cryptographic systems today use random number generators to produce secure keys.
But how do you know that a random number is truly random?
Classical computer algorithms can only create pseudorandom numbers, and someone with enough knowledge of the algorithm or the system could manipulate it or predict the next number. An expert in sleight of hand could rig a coin flip to guarantee a heads or tails result. Even the most careful coin flips can have bias; with enough study, their outcomes could be predicted.
"True
randomness
is something that nothing in the universe can predict in advance," said Krister Shalm, a physicist at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Even if a random number generator used seemingly random processes in nature, it would be hard to verify that those numbers are truly random, Shalm added.
Einstein believed that nature isn't random, famously saying, "God does not play dice with the universe." Scientists have since proved that Einstein was wrong.
Unlike dice or computer algorithms,
quantum mechanics
is inherently random. Carrying out a quantum experiment called a Bell test, Shalm and his team have transformed this source of true quantum randomness into a traceable and certifiable random-number service.
"If God does play dice with the universe, then you can turn that into the best random number generator that the universe allows," Shalm said. "We really wanted to take that experiment out of the lab and turn it into a useful public service."
To make that happen, NIST researchers and their colleagues at the University of Colorado Boulder created the Colorado University Randomness Beacon (
CURBy
). CURBy produces
random numbers
automatically and broadcasts them daily through a website for anyone to use. The related research is
published
in the journal
Nature
.
At the heart of this service is the NIST-run Bell test, which provides truly random results. This randomness acts as a kind of raw material that the rest of the researchers' setup "refines" into random numbers published by the beacon.
The Bell test measures pairs of "entangled" photons whose properties are correlated even when separated by vast distances. When researchers measure an individual particle, the outcome is random, but the properties of the pair are more correlated than
classical physics
allows, enabling researchers to verify the randomness. Einstein called this quantum nonlocality "spooky action at a distance."
This is the first random number generator service to use quantum nonlocality as a source of its numbers, and the most transparent source of random numbers to date. That's because the results are certifiable and traceable to a greater extent than ever before.

"CURBy is one of the first publicly available services that operates with a provable quantum advantage. That's a big milestone for us," Shalm explained. "The quality and origin of these random bits can be directly certified in a way that conventional
random number generators
are unable to."
From left to right, Jasper Palfree University of Colorado Boulder), Gautam Kavuri (NIST) and Krister Shalm (NIST). Credit: NIST
NIST performed one of the first complete experimental Bell tests in 2015, which firmly established that
quantum mechanics is truly random
. In 2018, NIST pioneered methods to use these Bell tests to build
the world's first sources of true randomness.
However, turning these quantum correlations into random numbers is hard work. NIST's first breakthrough demonstrations of the Bell test required months of setup to run for a few hours, and it took a great deal of time to collect enough data to generate 512 bits of true randomness.

data.title: Sincerity Wins the War
data.author: treadump
data.article_summary: 《Sincerity Wins The War》由Edward Zitron撰写，强调新闻报道中的真诚和责任感。作者推出了付费新闻通讯，同时承诺继续提供免费内容。文章批评传统商业报道缺乏情感和诚实，主张在报道中加入背景和分析，而不仅仅是陈述事实。作者以Meta与军事承包商Anduril的合作为例，指出媒体对Meta和其“元宇宙”概念的过度炒作，并质疑Meta将不成熟的人工智能技术（如Llama）用于军事头盔的合理性。文章呼吁媒体对科技公司保持批判态度，并反思他们所报道的内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对报道中的主观性、AI和市场的 hype 以及对技术术语的讨论

不同观点：
• [bananalychee] 认为文章作者虽主张报道应体现“真诚”并考虑“背景”，但实际上却在选择性呈现符合自己世界观的背景，存在双重标准和确认偏误。作者批评记者在回顾时容易指出错误，但自己却也犯了同样的错误，比如过度强调某些数据而忽视其他数据。此外，他质疑这篇文章如何通过编辑审核。

• [JohnMakin] 讨论了市场对于AI等新技术的反应，认为市场往往被视为不会犯错，尤其在公司业绩上升和CEO宣传产品时。这种逻辑忽略了市场曾多次犯错，且这种推理是循环的，过分关注表面成功而忽视背后的实际操作。

• [MisterKent] 表达了对AI hype的不满，将其比作dotcom泡沫，认为AI的过度炒作正在损害对其他有价值技术的投资。他提到AI在实际工作中并未达到宣传的效果，反而产生了负面影响，如降低劳动成本、增加不可靠的信息以及减少对专业性和创造力的重视。他希望泡沫尽快破裂，以便回归理性发展。

• [tptacek] 质疑这篇文章与Zitron在6月9日的文章内容是否有实质区别，暗示可能存在观点重复或缺乏新意。

• [KerrAvon] 支持文章中现实主义的观点，但对术语“agents”的使用提出异议，认为技术上使用“bots”更合适。他引用历史，指出“agents”一词在技术领域有其合理性和历史背景。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是报道中的主观性和双重标准问题，尤其是如何平衡背景信息的呈现和避免偏见。
• 对AI技术及其市场炒作的看法存在明显分歧，一部分人认为AI的 hype 对投资和实际应用产生了负面影响，期待市场调整。
• 对技术术语的使用存在不同意见，反映出在技术讨论中，术语的选择和定义也可能引发争议。

44291189.article_content:
Sincerity Wins The War
Edward Zitron
Jun 16, 2025
33 min read
Hello Where’s Your Ed At Subscribers! I’ve started a premium version of this newsletter with a weekly Friday column where I go over the most meaningful news and give my views, which I guess is what you’d expect. Anyway, it’s $7 a month or $70 a year, and helps support the newsletter. I will continue to do my big free column too! Thanks.
What wins the war is sincerity.
What wins the war is accountability.
And we do not have to buy into the inevitability of this movement.
Nor do we have to cover it in the way it has always been covered. Why not mix emotion and honesty with business reporting? Why not pry apart the narrative as you tell the story rather than hoping the audience works it out? Forget “hanging them with their own rope” — describe what’s happening and hold these people accountable in the way you would be held accountable at your job.
Your job is not to report “the facts” and let the readers work it out. To quote my buddy Kasey, if you're not reporting the context, you're not reporting the story. Facts without context aren’t really facts. Blandly repeating what an executive or politician says and thinking that appending it with “...said [person]” is sufficient to communicate their biases or intentions isn’t just
irresponsible,
it’s actively rejecting your position as a journalist.
You don’t even have to say somebody is lying when they say they’re going to do something — but the word “allegedly” is powerful, reasonable and honest, and is an objective way of calling into question a narrative.
Let me give you a few examples.
A few weeks ago, multiple outlets reported that Meta would partner with Anduril, the military contractor founded by Palmer Luckey, the former founder of VR company Oculus which
Meta acquired in 2014
, only to
oust Luckey four years later for donating $10,000 to an anti-Hilary Clinton group
. In 2024, Meta CTO Andrew “Boz” Bosworth, famous for saying that Facebook’s growth is necessary and good, even if it leads to bad things like cyberbullying and  terror attacks,
publicly apologized to Luckey
.
Now the circle is completing, with
Luckey sort-of-returning to Meta to work with the company
on some sort of helmet called “Eagle Eye.”
One might think at this point the media would be a little more hesitant in how they cover anything Zuckerberg-related after he completely lied to them about the metaverse, and one would be wrong.
The Washington Post reported
that, and I quote:
To aid the collaboration, Meta will draw on its hefty investments in AI models known as Llama and its virtual reality division, Reality Labs. The company has built several iterations of immersive headsets aimed at blending the physical and virtual worlds — a concept known as the metaverse.
Are you
fucking kidding me?
The metaverse was a joke! It never existed! Meta bought a company that made VR headsets — a technology so old, they
featured in an episode of
Murder She Wrote
— and an online game that could best be described as “Second Life, but sadder.”
Here’s a piece from the Washington Post agreeing with me
! The metaverse never really had a product of any kind, and
lost tens of billions of dollars for no reason
!
Here’s a whole thing I wrote about it years ago
! To still bring up the metaverse in the year of our lord 2025 is ridiculous!
But even putting that aside… wait, Meta’s going to put
its
AI
inside
of this headset? Palmer Luckey claims that, according to the Post, this headset will be “combining an AI assistant with communications and other functions.” Llama? That assistant?
You mean the one that it had to rig to cheat on LLM benchmarking tests
? The one that will, as reported by the Wall Street Journal,
participate in vivid and gratuitous sexual fantasies
with children
? The one using generative AI models that hallucinate, like every other LLM? That’s the one that you’re gonna put in the helmet for the military? How is the helmet going to do that exactly? What will an LLM — an inconsistent and unreliable generative AI system — do in a combat situation, and will a soldier trust it again after its first fuckup?
Just to be clear, and I quote Palmer Luckey, the helmet that will feature an “ever-present companion who can operate systems, who can communicate with others, who you can off-load tasks onto … that is looking out for you with more eyes than you could ever look out for yourself right there right there in your helmet.”
This is all going to be powered by Llama?
Really?
Are we all really going to accept that? Does nobody actually think about the words they’re writing down?
Here’s the thing about military tech: the US DOD tends to be fairly conservative when it comes to the software it uses, and has high requirements for reliability and safety. I could talk about these for hours — from coding guidelines, to the ADA programming language, which was designed to be highly crash-resistant and powers everything from guided missiles to F-15 fighter jet —

• [JohnMakin] 讨论了市场对于AI等新技术的反应，认为市场往往被视为不会犯错，尤其在公司业绩上升和CEO宣传产品时。这种逻辑忽略了市场曾多次犯错，且这种推理是循环的，过分关注表面成功而忽视背后的实际操作。

• [MisterKent] 表达了对AI hype的不满，将其比作dotcom泡沫，认为AI的过度炒作正在损害对其他有价值技术的投资。他提到AI在实际工作中并未达到宣传的效果，反而产生了负面影响，如降低劳动成本、增加不可靠的信息以及减少对专业性和创造力的重视。他希望泡沫尽快破裂，以便回归理性发展。

• [tptacek] 质疑这篇文章与Zitron在6月9日的文章内容是否有实质区别，暗示可能存在观点重复或缺乏新意。

• [KerrAvon] 支持文章中现实主义的观点，但对术语“agents”的使用提出异议，认为技术上使用“bots”更合适。他引用历史，指出“agents”一词在技术领域有其合理性和历史背景。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是报道中的主观性和双重标准问题，尤其是如何平衡背景信息的呈现和避免偏见。
• 对AI技术及其市场炒作的看法存在明显分歧，一部分人认为AI的 hype 对投资和实际应用产生了负面影响，期待市场调整。
• 对技术术语的使用存在不同意见，反映出在技术讨论中，术语的选择和定义也可能引发争议。

data.title: Amazon Signs 141,000 Square Foot Silicon Valley We Work Lease Amid RTO Mandate
data.author: randycupertino
data.article_summary: 亚马逊（Amazon）在硅谷签署了14.1万平方英尺的WeWork办公空间租赁协议，以支持其重返办公室工作的政策。该办公地点位于加州圣克拉拉，亚马逊将整栋大楼用于其员工的全职现场工作。由于此前亚马逊在达拉斯、凤凰城、亚特兰大和纽约等地面临办公空间不足的问题，此次扩展旨在解决这些需求。公司CEO安迪·贾西（Andy Jassy）强调，面对面协作对公司运营至关重要。此外，亚马逊还计划在宾夕法尼亚州投资至少200亿美元，建设云计算和人工智能园区，创造至少1250个高薪技术岗位。尽管重返办公室政策面临通勤和停车等挑战，亚马逊仍坚定推进其办公空间扩展计划。

  - [x0x0] 分享了个人在WeWork工作的负面体验，指出其玻璃墙和硬木地板虽然视觉上吸引人，但在实际使用中缺乏声音隔离，导致工作环境嘈杂，尤其是回声问题严重，进一步强调了相比开放式设计，传统的小隔间和吸音地毯反而更实用。

) office expansion knows no bounds. Fresh from

, the tech giant announced it is growing its presence in Silicon Valley by teaming up with WeWork (NYSE:

CoStar News
reports.
The new offices are located at 4980 Great America Parkway in Santa Clara, California, in a building that Amazon will occupy in its entirety as part of its effort to have its workforce return to a five-day-per-week in-office work schedule.
“We’re constantly evaluating our office footprint based on the needs of Amazon’s businesses,” an Amazon spokesperson told CoStar News.

WeWork Works In A Tariff-Wary Climate

recent summit
. “You have to think about it. You have to think whether or not to invest that major capital in a market, at least through this short term. You have to step back,”
he told Bloomberg
.

Amazon Has Lacked Office Space For Returning Workers
While back-to-work mandates have been popular amongst
many major corporations
this year, Amazon has struggled to implement their’s due to a lack of office space. Workers in
Dallas, Phoenix, Atlanta and New York
had their deadlines to return to the office pushed back four months while Amazon acquired more space.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy
told employees in September
that returning to an in-office work regimen was vital because “collaborating, brainstorming and inventing are simpler and more effective.”

“If it’s not for you, then that’s OK. You can go and find another company if you want to. But for us, that’s what we’ve decided is the best way to operate our company,” Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said at a
Wall Street Journal
event in October.

.
Parking And Commuting Are Problems For Returning Workers
The return-to-office push has not been without its complications, with parking space and commuting being among the complaints from former remote workers, the Journal reported.
“While we’ve heard ideas for improvement from a relatively small number of employees and are working to address those, these anecdotes don’t reflect the sentiment we’re hearing from most of our teammates,” a company spokeswoman told the Journal in February. “What we’re seeing is great energy across our offices.”
The Largest Capital Investment In Pennsylvania
On June 9 Pennsylvania Gov.
Josh Shapiro announced
that Amazon planned to invest “at least $20 billion to establish multiple high-tech cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) innovation campuses across the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.” The push would create “at least 1,250 high-paying, high-tech jobs. Salem Township and Falls Township are the first communities identified as sites for these future campuses,” he said in a statement. It marks the largest capital investment in the commonwealth’s history.

data.title: Canyon.mid
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Tandy 1000 RSX电脑及其相关技术（如MIDI、声卡、老式计算机设备）的讨论

不同观点：
• **Dwedit** 对YouTube视频中错误地将Tandy 1000 RSX（1991年款，具备Super VGA图形能力）与早期的Tandy图形和Adlib或Sound Blaster声卡联系在一起表示不满。他指出，虽然RSX只有一个ISA槽，用户可以自行安装声卡，但它本身并未配备这些功能。

• **Disposal8433** 分享个人经历，提到自己过去由于没有声卡，只能用PC喇叭玩游戏（尤其是LucasArts的游戏），并认为MIDI版本的音乐缺乏PC喇叭的“原始电力感”。

• **zkmon** 反思技术的发展，认为过去的计算机在游戏、娱乐和生产力方面已经足够，但“足够”的定义不断变化，像是在追逐一个永远无法完全达到的目标。

• **theletterf** 提供资源，提到Canyon.mid的创作者George Stone曾在一个采访中被提及，并附上链接。

• **p1mrx** 对视频文件大小比MIDI文件大100倍表示惊讶。

• **tgv** 分享过去制造商为合成器键盘和模块创建的演示歌曲，并提供多个YouTube链接作为例子，指出这是当时的一种潮流。

• **fishgoesblub** 对YouTube视频播放器未禁用控制功能表示不满，因未调节音量导致被突然的音量吓到。

• **kelvie** 讨论MIDI播放的复杂性，提到在Linux系统上播放MIDI文件需要做出许多选择和安装额外程序，而过去在Windows Media Player上可以直接播放，感到怀念。

• **esafak** 分享Sound Blaster声卡带来的音质提升体验，将其比喻为从黑白电视到彩色电视的飞跃。

• **b0a04gl** 欣赏老式计算机设备的稳定性和延续性，认为这些设备教会了用户耐心，并提供了与投入相称的回报。

• **torcete** 喜欢Windows 3.1/3.11的GUI，认为其简洁、清晰、快速，相比之下后来的界面显得臃肿和低效。

• **hliyan** 回忆起旧Sony录音机附带的演示磁带，提到一段无法找到的乐曲，表达怀旧情绪。

• **burnt-resistor** 指出MIDI文件在不同声卡上的播放效果不同，因为不同声卡的波表、音色库和MIDI芯片不同，因此没有统一的MIDI文件播放效果。

• **pyromaker** 怀念过去的技术时代，认为虽然过去技术更手动、繁琐、更多bug，但也更具创造性和可配置性，表达对旧时代的怀念。

• **layer8** 认为图片中的Zip驱动器稍微有些时代错位，尽管它在Windows 95发布前几个月推出，但仍感到有些不协调。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在老式计算机设备和技术的准确性和怀旧情绪上，例如Tandy 1000 RSX是否自带声卡、MIDI播放的复杂性以及过去技术是否真的比现代技术更“真实”或更“有趣”。

• 讨论中多次提到怀旧和对过去技术的欣赏，反映出参与者对技术发展过程中失去的一些特性的怀念。

• 不同用户对音质、设备功能和过去体验的看法各异，但普遍认同过去技术有一些独特的魅力和教育意义。

data.title: GitHub CI/CD observability with OpenTelemetry step by step guide
data.author: ankit01-oss
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了如何使用OpenTelemetry为GitHub Actions的CI/CD管道增加可观察性。OpenTelemetry是一个开源的可观察性框架，能够以标准、供应商无关的方式收集 traces、metrics 和 logs。文章解释了为何要使用 OpenTelemetry 观察 CI/CD 管道，包括实现端到端可见性、性能优化、错误检测与调试，以及依赖分析等优势。通过配置 OpenTelemetry Collector 和 GitHub Receiver，可以捕获工作流事件作为 traces，并通过 GitHub API 获取 metrics。文章还提供了具体的设置步骤，包括配置 GitHub 网络钩子和访问令牌，以实现对 GitHub Actions 的全面监控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenTelemetry（OTel）在不同场景下的使用及其与其他 observability 工具（如 SigNoz、CloudWatch、Sentry）的比较

不同观点：
• **hrpnk** 对 OTel 是否适合长时间运行的批处理/异步进程表示疑问，尤其是与单体应用构建的对比，关注点在于 OTel 是否适合处理耗时较长的任务。
  
• **reactordev** 认为 OTel 虽然很棒，但一旦选择了某个路径，切换会非常痛苦。他建议如果使用 AWS，CloudWatch 是更好的选择，因为 AWS 拥有更多数据，能提供更好的体验。同时，如果拥有自己的基础设施，SigNoz 也是不错的选择。

• **totetsu** 分享了自己通过 GitHub Actions 和 API 调用的经验，尝试将过程追踪发送到 Jaeger 或 Grafana，以获得性能的可视化视图。他还提到从 runner 主机监控日志文件的潜在方法，但认为 API 提供的信息更详细。

补充讨论：
• OTel 的切换成本高，选择时需谨慎。
• 对于在 AWS 上运行的应用，CloudWatch 因其数据优势可能更适合。
• Sentry 作为替代方案的优缺点，特别是在集成便利性和供应商锁定问题上。
• SigNoz 的付费功能和开放核心模式的讨论。
• 实际操作中通过 API 调用获取详细信息的可行性，及 OTel 在文件支持方面的不足。

争议焦点：
• OTel 是否适合长时间运行的批处理/异步进程。
• 不同 observability 工具（如 OTel、SigNoz、CloudWatch、Sentry）之间的选择及其优劣对比。

CI/CD Observability with OpenTelemetry - A Step by Step Guide
Author:
Elizabeth Mathew
In the fast-paced world of CI/CD, understanding the performance and behaviour of your pipelines is crucial. GitHub Actions has become a popular choice for automating builds and deployments, but anyone who's debugged a flaky workflow or long-running job knows how challenging it can be to get visibility into what's happening under the hood. We usually rely on build logs, timing data, or guesswork when something goes wrong.
Wouldn't it be nice to trace a pipeline run step-by-step, or have metrics on how your workflows are performing over time?
This is where OpenTelemetry comes into play.
OpenTelemetry [OTel]
is an open-source observability framework that enables collecting traces, metrics, and logs in a standard, vendor-agnostic way. With a bit of configuration, OTel can capture telemetry from even our CI/CD pipelines. In this guide, we'll walk through setting up OpenTelemetry for GitHub Actions [covering both tracing and metrics], with practical examples and configuration snippets.
Why Observe CI/CD Pipelines with OpenTelemetry [OTel]?
Just as we use traces and metrics to understand microservices and applications, we can apply the same to CI/CD pipelines. Instrumenting GitHub Actions with OpenTelemetry yields several benefits:
End-to-end visibility:
You can trace the entire lifecycle of a workflow run, from trigger to completion. Each job and step can be visualised, showing how they execute and interact.
Performance optimisation:
By measuring the duration of each job and step, you can identify bottlenecks or slow steps in your pipeline.
For example, a long testing phase or a slow dependency installation.
Error detection and debugging:
Traces can pinpoint exactly where a workflow failed or took an unexpected path, making it easier to debug broken pipelines. Instead of combing through logs, you'll see which step or action resulted in an error.
Dependency analysis:
In complex workflows with multiple jobs [possibly with dependencies or concurrent runs], tracing helps you understand how different jobs and steps relate to each other within the workflow.
Traditionally, engineering teams have monitored CI pipelines using ad-hoc methods, maybe exporting build logs to an ELK stack, timing data to Prometheus, or using CI-specific analytics. Those approaches often cover only metrics [like durations, success/failure counts] or logs. OpenTelemetry provides a unified approach, it can capture
traces
[for structure and timing] and
metrics
[for quantitative monitoring] in one system.
Every pipeline run can become a trace, and important KPIs can be emitted as metrics using OTel. Next, we'll see how to set this up with GitHub Actions.
How OpenTelemetry Captures GitHub Actions Data
To make GitHub Actions observable with OTel, we leverage a component of the OTel Collector known as the
GitHub Receiver
. This receiver can do some very cool things like,
Ingest GitHub workflow events as traces:
GitHub can send events [via webhooks] whenever workflows run or jobs execute. The GitHub Receiver accepts these events and converts them into trace data.
Scrape GitHub metrics via the API:
The same receiver can use GitHub's APIs [GraphQL and REST] to scrape repository and workflow-related metrics. This includes information like
repository size, star count, open pull requests, issue counts, contributor statistics
, and more.
📝
Note
We can set intervals at which scraping should take place when configuring the receiver as shown below:
github
:
initial_delay
:
1s
collection_interval
:
60s
In the sections below, we'll go through the steps to configure the OpenTelemetry Collector with the GitHub receiver for both traces and metrics.
Setting Up the OpenTelemetry Collector for GitHub Actions Observability
Okay. Let's dive into the setup.
Step 0: Updating Your GitHub Config
On the GitHub side of things, you'll need to set up a webhook on your repository [or organization] that sends
workflow_run
and
workflow_job
events to your Collector endpoint. In GitHub's settings, add a new webhook and select at least these two event types, with the content type set to
application/json
.
We will configure the Collector to listen for these events on a specific URL. You'll also need a secret token for the webhook [a random string] to secure it; the Collector will use the same secret to validate incoming events.
For metrics, if you want to scrape data from the GitHub API, you'll need an access token with permissions to read repo and workflow data. You can read this
guide
to understand how to get your personal access token.
Configure your GitHub webhook
With that in place, let's set up the Collector step by step.
Step 1: Install/ Update the OTel Collector
If you haven't already, install the OpenTelemetry Collector [we'll use the
otelcol-contrib
distribution because the GitHub receiver is part of the contrib components

data.title: An origin trial for a new HTML <permission> element (2024)
data.author: tentacleuno
data.article_summary: Chrome团队正在试验一种新的HTML `<permission>`元素，作为声明式请求权限的方法，以解决当前命令式请求权限所面临的多种挑战。当前，网站通过命令式方法（如`navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()`或`Notification.requestPermission()`）请求权限，但这种方法导致了权限滥用（如未经用户交互就弹出提示）和用户体验问题（如提示被忽略或难以撤销决定）。为解决这些问题，Chrome引入了`<permission>`元素，旨在让开发者更清晰地声明所需权限，并计划在Chrome 126中进行初步试验，最终推动其标准化。这一新方法旨在简化权限请求流程，改善用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google提出的`<permission>`元素标准及其在浏览器中的实现，涉及权限请求的UI设计、用户信任、安全问题以及与其他浏览器厂商的讨论和争议。

不同观点：
• **对Google动机的质疑**：[account-5] 担心Google推动此提案的动机，认为Google可能通过这种方式削弱权限提示的明确性，从而为自己的广告业务谋利。他提到Manifest 3和Passkey等例子，认为这些改动表面上是为了安全和用户体验，但实际上可能对Google自身业务更有利。

• **权限提示UI设计的争议**：[RainyDayTmrw] 和 [mbo] 提到了“死亡线”（line of death）的概念，认为权限提示应该与网页内容明确区分，以确保用户能够信任浏览器的UI，而不是被网站误导。他们担心新的提案会让权限请求变得更容易被网站伪装或混淆，从而削弱浏览器的安全保障。[b0a04gl] 进一步指出，将权限请求嵌入网页内容可能改变用户对信任的感知，长期来看会增加用户判断的难度。

• **技术实现和安全问题**：[afavour] 和 [cwillu] 担心内嵌权限提示的技术实现问题，特别是防止点击劫持（clickjacking）等安全问题。他们认为限制内嵌提示的样式虽然可以避免一些问题，但可能导致开发者使用变通方法，从而带来更多的维护难题。[notnullorvoid] 直接指出，权限提示应该完全由浏览器控制，而不是由网页控制，以确保用户信任。

• **提案的设计缺陷和改进建议**：[JimDabell] 和 [blue_pants] 认为提案的声明式设计和实际需要的操作不一致，并未解决权限请求的“难以撤销”问题。他们建议让浏览器定义UI，确保网站无法遮蔽或篡改权限请求。同时，[GrantMoyer] 指出Google的试验缺少“永久阻止”选项，可能对用户控制权限造成不便。

补充讨论：
• **标准化的争议**：[madeofpalk] 提到Chrome团队正在寻求各浏览器厂商的正式立场，但Firefox和WebKit目前反对此提案。这表明该提案在标准化过程中面临阻力。[Robdel12] 批评Google绕过标准流程直接推出API的做法，认为这可能会导致混乱。

• **提案的时间问题**：[cprecioso] 提到这个提案和试验其实已经有一年多，且试验已经结束，但讨论仍在继续，表明社区对该提案的实际效果和影响仍有疑虑。

争议焦点：Google提出的`<permission>`元素是否会削弱权限请求的明确性和用户信任，以及是否主要为Google自身业务利益服务。同时，技术实现上的安全问题和标准化过程中的分歧也是争议的核心。

44281633.article_content:
Chrome for Developers
Blog
An origin trial for a new HTML <permission> element
Stay organized with collections
Save and categorize content based on your preferences.
Thomas Steiner
GitHub
Glitch
LinkedIn
Mastodon
Bluesky
Homepage
There are a number of
imperative
methods for asking for permission to use
powerful features like location access in web apps. These methods come with a
number of challenges, which is why the Chrome permissions team is experimenting
with a new
declarative
method: a dedicated HTML
<permission>
element. This
element is in origin trial from Chrome 126, and ultimately we hope to
standardize it.
Imperative methods for requesting permission
When web apps need access to
powerful features
, they
need to ask for permission. For example, when
Google Maps
requires the user's location using the
Geolocation API
,
browsers will prompt the user, often with the option to store that decision.
This is a
well defined concept
in the Permissions specification.
Implicitly ask on first use versus explicitly request upfront
The Geolocation API is a powerful API and relies on the implicitly ask on first
use approach. For example, when an app calls the
navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()
method, the permissions prompt automatically pops up upon the first call.
Another example is
navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()
.
Other APIs, like the
Notification API
or
the
Device Orientation and Motion API
,
commonly have an explicit way to request permission through a static method like
Notification.requestPermission()
or
DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()
.
Note:
Historically, there were plans for yet another way to get permission,
namely an explicit
navigator.permissions.request()
method, but it was removed
from the Permissions API following the discussion in
Issue #83
in the specification's
repository. The question of the "right" approach between these methods
(implicitly prompt upon use and explicitly request permission) is a much
discussed topic without a clear answer.
Challenges with imperative methods for asking for permission
Permission spam
In the past, websites could call methods like
navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()
or
Notification.requestPermission()
,
but also
navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()
immediately when a website
was loaded. A permission prompt would pop up before the user had interacted with
the website. This is sometimes described as permission spam and affects both
approaches, implicitly asking on first use as well as explicitly requesting
upfront.
Browser mitigations and user gesture requirement
Permission spam led to browser vendors requiring a user gesture like a button
click or a keydown event before showing a permission prompt. The problem with
this approach is that it's very difficult, if not impossible, for the browser to
figure out if a given user gesture should result in a permission prompt to be
shown or not. Maybe the user was just clicking on the page in frustration
anywhere because the page took so long to load, or maybe they were indeed
clicking on the
Locate me
button. Some websites also became very good at
tricking users into clicking on content to trigger the prompt.
Another mitigation is adding prompt abuse mitigations, like completely blocking
features to begin with, or to showing the permission prompt in a non-modal, less
intrusive manner.
Permission contextualization
Another challenge, especially on big screens, is the way the permission prompt
gets commonly displayed: above the
line of death
, that
is, outside of the area of the browser window that the app can draw onto. It's
not unheard of that users would miss the prompt at the top of their browser
window when they just clicked a button at the bottom of the window. This problem
is often exacerbated when browser spam mitigations are in place.
No easy undo
Finally, it is too easy for users to navigate themselves into a dead-end. For
example, once the user has blocked access to a feature, it requires them to be
aware of the site information drop-down where they can either
Reset
permissions
or toggle blocked permissions back on. Both options in the worst
case require a full reload of the page until the updated setting takes effect.
Sites have no ability to provide an easy shortcut for users to change an
existing permission state and have to painstakingly explain to users how to
change their settings as shown at the bottom of the following Google Maps
screenshot.
If the permission is key to the experience, for example, microphone access for a
video conferencing application, apps like Google Meet show intrusive dialogs
that instruct the user how to unblock the permission.
A declarative
<permission>
element
To address the challenges described in this post, the Chrome permissions team
have launched an origin trial for a new HTML element,
<permission>
. This
element lets developers declaratively ask for permission to use, for now, a
subset of the powerful features available to websites. In its simplest form

data.title: WhatsApp is getting ads using personal data from Instagram and Facebook
data.author: ThePhysicist
data.article_summary: Meta计划在WhatsApp上引入基于Facebook和Instagram个人数据的广告，进一步整合其服务，扩大广告收入。这违反了欧盟的《数字市场法》(DMA)和《通用数据保护条例》(GDPR)中关于用户"自由给予的同意"的要求。Meta目前在其平台上采用"付费或同意"模式，用户若不想看广告需付费，但这并未真正提供选择自由。欧盟法律对此似乎缺乏有效 enforcement，引发了新的法律争议。隐私权益组织noyb表示将对Meta采取法律行动，并预测用户可能转向Signal等非盈利通讯应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟《数字市场法》(DMA) 实施后，第三方消息应用的互通整合问题

不同观点：
• [支持互通整合的观点]  
   ◦ 支持者认为，根据《数字市场法》(DMA) 的规定，大型平台应该允许第三方应用的互通，特别是在消息传递方面。  
   ◦ 举例：用户可以在WhatsApp上直接与Telegram用户通讯，无需切换应用。这将提升用户体验，打破信息孤岛。

• [质疑互通整合的可行性]  
   ◦ 质疑者认为，消息应用的互通在技术上可能非常复杂，涉及到不同平台间的协议、数据格式、安全性等问题。

44289181.article_content:
WhatsApp is getting ads using personal data from Instagram and Facebook
Forced Consent & Consent Bypass
/
16 June 2025
Meta announced today that it also wants to introduce ads on WhatsApp, which will be based on personal data from Facebook and Instagram. This further integrates WhatsApp into other Meta services - an originally independent app, which initially was available for just $1 per year without ads or data usage. This also means that Meta is consolidating its social networking monopoly. EU law was actually supposed to prevent this.
Meta's announcement
Report by TechCrunch
Probably not legal: DMA and GDPR.
When Meta bought WhatsApp in 2014, there were fears of a merger and an increase of the company's monopoly power. The
EU Commission waved through
Meta's purchase of WhatsApp nonetheless. Now, with the new Digital Markets Act (DMA) in place, the EU pledged to restrict the dominance of big tech monopolies. Article 5(2) of the DMA requires freely given user consent when companies want to link data across services. Similarly, the GDPR requires
“freely given”
consent for personalised advertising. Users should therefore have the option to say
"yes"
or
"no"
. However, Meta does not currently allow this on Instagram and Facebook. Instead, it has introduced a so-called Pay or Okay model, where users have to pay if they want to say
"no"
to ads. It would be likely that Meta takes the same approach on WhatsApp.
"Pay or Okay" also on WhatsApp?
Given that EU law requires consent, the question arises how Meta wants to implement that? Until 2016, WhatsApp had cost US$1 per year. In the meantime,
Meta charges € 9.99
for using Instagram or Facebook without ads (that is €119.88 per year or 120 times the old WhatsApp fee). The
EU Commission has already classified Meta's Pay or Okay approach as illegal
– but so far, Meta is happily continuing (with minimal changes) to force a fee on users that do not want give up their right to privacy. While only about 3-10% of people want personalised advertising, Pay or Okay gives Meta a consent-rate of more than 99% – just not
“freely given”
, but through excessive fees if you don't give up your data. It is likely that Meta would take the same approach when implementing data sharing and advertisement on WhatsApp. This yields a lot of profit, while operating a messaging app is not expensive: The popular alternative Signal only needs a
budget of $50 million
to run a global non-profit alternative.
Max Schrems, chairman of noyb:
"Meta is doing exactly the opposite of what EU law requires. The data of its various platforms gets linked and users are tracked for advertising without any genuine choice. Without freely given consent, linking data and showing personalised advertising is clearly illegal. Meta has already introduced a 'Pay or Okay' approach on Instagram and Facebook, without the Irish data protection authority or the EU Commission taking any effective action against it. We suspect that Meta will do the same with WhatsApp."
EU laws finally irrelevant for Meta?
While WhatsApp is hardly used in Meta's home market in the US, it is very dominant in the rest of the world. The largest global market for WhatsApp in terms of purchasing power is certainly the EU. Nevertheless, since Donald Trump's election, Meta seems to have changed course and is openly ignoring EU law. Like the Trump administration, Meta has now adopted the narrative that existing EU law would be an unfair trade barrier for US big tech
and "almost like a tariff"
. A few weeks ago, Meta announced that it would use the personal data of all EU users for AI training without asking for consent. Now comes the next blow: using that data for ads on WhatsApp. Meta no longer seems to care about what Brussels legislates.
Max Schrems: "
The lack of enforcement of EU law is painfully obvious. The EU Commission and national data protection authorities have a duty to protect citizens from the use of their data without consent – but Meta learned that there are no real consequences. There are hardly any penalties, and the penalties that have been imposed so far have not been paid. Instead, Meta seems to follow the approach by the Trump administration and simply ignores EU rules as somehow 'illegitimate'. European regulators urgently need to take clear action.
"
Next legal battle on the horizon.
noyb
will, of course, examine this breach of the law again. If necessary, we will initiate procedures against Meta. The details depend on Meta's practical implementation and therefore cannot yet be assessed conclusively.
Max Schrems: “
Signal works just as well as WhatsApp, but is non-profit and donation-funded. We expect that Meta's push to show ads on WhatsApp will lead to the next big exodus to Signal.”

data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 日本计划投入约7亿美元（¥1000亿）吸引海外科研人才，尤其是因特朗普政府削减科研预算和限制学术自由而感到不安的美国研究人员。该计划旨在打造精英研究环境，特别是在人工智能和半导体领域，与全球人才竞争。日本 Tohoku 大学也将投入约2亿美元招募500名研究人员。此前，欧洲委员会也宣布了类似的"选择欧洲"计划，投资5.66亿美元吸引研究人员。英国议会也正讨论吸引美国学术人才的措施。与此同时，日本通过 Rapidus 公司大力发展国内半导体制造，进一步增强对科研人才的吸引力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲与日本、美国在学术人才和研发投资方面的竞争力比较

不同观点：
• [kryptiskt] 认为欧洲应设立基金支持本地学术人才，而不是依赖于通过在国外获得经验后再被高薪挖回的方式来吸引人才。他对欧洲目前的做法表示不满，质疑是否一定要去美国工作才能获得高薪和认可。

• [comrade1234] 提到欧盟已经宣布了5亿美元的基金来解决此问题，并指出微软在瑞士投资了4亿美元用于云计算。然而，他认为5亿美元的资金规模相对较小，可能效果有限，暗示这些投资可能不足以改变现状。

• [alephnerd] 认为日本的举措会比欧洲的更成功。他指出，日本已经成为中韩白领的重要目的地，尤其是在材料科学等领域，并且日本经济产业省在研发推广和商业化方面更具实力。他还提到，欧洲的研发计划往往因为欧盟和国家层面之间的灰色地带而难以推进，并建议欧洲领导人需要明确优先考虑欧盟整体还是 individual 国家。此外，他认为欧洲的中档大学（如艾克斯-马赛大学或巴斯大学）无法与日本的名校（如东北大学）竞争。

补充讨论：
• 资金的有效性：[comrade1234] 对5亿美元基金的效果持怀疑态度，尤其是与私营部门的投资（如微软的4亿美元投资）相比。
• 日本与欧洲的对比：[alephnerd] 强调日本在吸引东亚人才和研发商业化方面的优势，并认为这是欧洲需要改进的地方。
• 欧盟内部的协调问题：[alephnerd] 指出欧盟和国家层面在研发计划上的不协调是影响其成功的重要因素。
• 欧美人才流动：[kryptiskt] 对欧美之间的人才流动表示不满，认为欧洲应更好地留住本地人才。

争议焦点：
• 欧盟5亿美元基金是否足够：[comrade1234] 认为资金不足，而其他观点未直接回应这一点。
• 欧洲大学与日本大学竞争力的比较：[alephnerd] 认为欧洲的中档大学无法与日本的顶尖大学竞争，这一观点可能引起争议，特别是对于欧洲学术界的支持者而言。

44291322.article_content:
Science
2
Japan builds near $700M fund to lure foreign academic talent
2
For researchers yearning to earn some yen and escape Trump 2.0
Dan Robinson
Mon 16 Jun 2025
//
16:26 UTC
Japan is the latest nation hoping to tempt disgruntled US researchers alarmed by the Trump administration's hostile attitude to academia to relocate to the Land of the Rising Sun.
The Japanese government aims to create an elite research environment, and has detailed a ¥100 billion ($693 million) package to attract researchers from abroad, including those from America who may have seen their budgets slashed or who fear a clampdown on their academic freedom.
American science put on starvation diet
READ MORE
Kyodo News Plus
said the measures are in recognition of the growing global competition to attract the best talent, in fields such as artificial intelligence and semiconductors. It isn't therefore aimed at just researchers from the US, but they are seen as a key target.
This is because the Trump administration making a number of
cuts to scientific funding
in America, including to the
NASA budget
and the
National Science Foundation
, and has specifically targeted
diversity and equality
efforts.
Minoru Kiuchi, Japan's Minister in charge of Economic Security, said: "We will make utmost efforts to make our country the most attractive in the world for researchers." He also serves as Minister of State for Science and Technology Policy.
This new policy package is expected to fund various programs, including a plan by Tohoku University in Sendai to spend around ¥30 billion ($208 million) to recruit about 500 researchers from Japan and abroad.
Japan's move follows an
announcement in May from the European Commission
(EC) that it wanted to make Europe the home of science by tempting researchers and scientists to relocate there.
The "
Choose Europe
" scheme is to include a €500 million ($566 million) package for 2025-2027 to make Europe "a magnet for researchers," with EC President Ursula von der Leyen saying it would promote the region as a world-leading center of research, innovation, and scientific freedom.
This came after the launch of the
Safe Place For Science
program by Aix-Marseille University in the south of France a month earlier. This was setup with the intention of offering a "safe and stimulating environment" for American researchers wishing to pursue their work free from persecution.
Not to be outdone, the geologically slow wheels of the British Parliament rolled into action, resulting in the Parliamentary Science, Innovation and Technology Committee
penning a letter to the Minister for Science Lord Patrick Vallance
, asking for more effort to lure disaffected US academics to Blighty.
Britain is hoping to attract ten specific classes of researchers, but the relevant scheme is only likely to get £50 million ($67 million) in funding.
Uncle Sam claims H-1B fraud crackdown is working as registrations drop 25%
US govt's science foundation purges 37 divisions, equity unit among casualties
Revenge of the nerds: Teachers, professors sue to undo Trump science funding cuts
Trump says US should kill CHIPS Act, use the cash to cut debt
Chinyelu "Chi" Onwurah, the Member of Parliament for Newcastle-upon-Tyne Central and West, called for the government to go further and deliver targeted support for scientists seeking to leave the US, and consider options such as relaxing visa requirements.
"Some universities in Europe have already begun to actively recruit researchers from the US, and countries such as Netherlands and Australia have set up funds to recruit top foreign scientists," wrote Onwurah.
However, Japan's plans to attract semiconductor talent could be boosted by the fact its government is already pouring billions into kick-starting advanced silicon manufacturing in the country via
Rapidus
, a company setup in 2022 with the goal of manufacturing 2nm chips by 2027. ®

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该信任Meta（Facebook母公司）处理与心理健康相关的事务

不同观点：
• 观点一：不信任Meta处理心理健康事务  
   支持这一观点的论据包括：Meta在隐私和数据保护方面有不良记录，用户担心其无法妥善保护敏感的健康数据。评论中提到“don’t trust Meta with your mental health”，暗示对Meta在心理健康领域的介入持怀疑态度。此外，有人可能认为科技公司缺乏专业知识，不应插手心理健康这种需要专业知识的领域。

• 观点二：Meta可能有能力处理心理健康事务  
   另一种观点认为，Meta作为大型科技公司，拥有丰富的数据资源和人工智能技术，或许能够通过数据分析和算法帮助用户监控和改善心理健康。支持者可能认为，科技公司可以利用其技术优势，开发出有效的工具来帮助用户管理心理健康问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：数据隐私与技术能力之间的平衡  
   一些人担心Meta在处理心理健康数据时可能会侵犯用户隐私，尤其是在过去有过泄露和不当使用用户数据的案例。另一方面，有人认为如果处理得当，Meta的技术能力可以在心理健康领域做出积极贡献。因此，争议的核心在于如何在利用技术优势的同时，确保用户数据的安全和隐私。

• 讨论扩展：心理健康服务的专业性  
   有评论可能提到心理健康服务需要高度的专业性，科技公司即便拥有技术优势，可能也无法替代专业的心理医生和医疗服务提供者。因此，一些人认为心理健康事务应由专业机构负责，而不是科技公司。

• 例子：过去的数据泄露和隐私丑闻  
   评论中可能提到剑桥分析丑闻等事件，作为不信任Meta处理敏感数据的例子，进一步支持不信任Meta的观点。这些事件加剧了公众对Meta处理用户数据能力的怀疑。

总结：讨论围绕是否应该信任Meta处理心理健康事务展开，主要分歧在于对其数据隐私保护能力和专业性的质疑，以及对其技术能力的认可。争议焦点在于如何平衡技术优势与隐私保护之间的关系。

   有评论可能提到心理健康服务需要高度的专业性，科技公司即便拥有技术优势，可能也无法替代专业的心理医生和医疗服务提供者。因此，一些人认为心理健康事务应由专业机构负责，而不是科技公司。

• 例子：过去的数据泄露和隐私丑闻  
   评论中可能提到剑桥分析丑闻等事件，作为不信任Meta处理敏感数据的例子，进一步支持不信任Meta的观点。这些事件加剧了公众对Meta处理用户数据能力的怀疑。

总结：讨论围绕是否应该信任Meta处理心理健康事务展开，主要分歧在于对其数据隐私保护能力和专业性的质疑，以及对其技术能力的认可。争议焦点在于如何平衡技术优势与隐私保护之间的关系。

data.title: Getting free internet on a cruise, saving $170
data.author: humanperhaps
data.article_summary: 文章描述了一位在游轮上的青少年通过技术手段获取免费上网的经历。游轮上的网络费用高昂，作者发现通过公主游轮（Princess Cruises）App可以获得15分钟的免费网络，且该免费时段与设备的MAC地址绑定。作者利用一台运行OpenWRT固件的旅行路由器，通过更改MAC地址重复获取免费网络。作者编写了一个Python脚本，自动执行更改MAC地址、登录MedallionNet及激活免费网络的步骤，并通过Docker容器实现自动刷新网络会话。最终，作者成功实现了在游轮上长时间免费上网，且网速与付费用户相当。文章还附上了作者的代码示例及实现方法。

44291630.article_content:
An image of two laptops, the one on the left accessing the internet for free and the one on the right having a $60/day connection. The router used to spoof the MAC address is connected to an Anker Zolo power bank.
Table of Contents
The script
Picture this, you’re a teenager in the middle of the ocean on a cruise ship. All is good, except you’re lacking your lifeblood: internet. You could pay $170 for seven days of throttled internet on a
single
device, and perhaps split it via a travel router or hotspot, but that still seems less than ideal.
I’ve been travelling Europe with family and am currently on Princess Cruises’ Sun Princess cruise ship. For the past two days, the ship has mostly been in port, so I was able to use a cellular connection. This quickly became not feasible as we got further from land, where there was no coverage. At around the same time, I wanted to download the Princess Cruises app on my phone, and realized that it would give me a
one-time 15-minute
internet connection. I activated it, and quickly realized that it didn’t limit you to just the Play Store or App Store: all websites could be accessed. I soon realized that this “one-time” download was MAC-address dependent and thus, could be bypassed by switching MAC addresses. However, doing so logs you out of the MedallionNet portal, which is required to get the 15-minutes of free internet.
This means that in order to get just 15 minutes of internet, the following is required:
Change MAC address
Login to MedallionNet with date-of-birth and room number, binding the MAC address to your identity
Send a request with your booking ID activating 15 minutes of free internet, intended to be used for downloading the Princess app
Not completely sure, but it did initially seem that to activate unrestricted access to the internet, you would need to send a simple HTTP to play.google.com, although I don’t think this is needed.
This process, on the surface, seems extremely arduous. But if this could be automated, it would suddenly become a much more viable proposition. After looking at the fetch requests the MedallionNet portal was sending to login and activate the free sessions, I realized that it shouldn’t be
too
hard to automate.
Conveniently, my family also brought a travel router running OpenWRT as we were planning on purchasing the throttled single-device plan (which is ~$170 for the entire cruise) and using the router as a hotspot so we could connect multiple devices to the internet. This router (a GL.iNet) allows you to change the MAC address via the admin portal, needing only a single POST request. This meant that if I could string together the API requests to change the MAC address (after getting a token from the router login endpoint), login to MedallionNet, and request the free internet session, I would have free internet.
I first tried copying the requests as cURL commands via DevTools into Notepad and using a local LLM to vibe-code a simple bash file. Realizing this wasn’t going to work, I began work on a Python script instead. I converted the cURL commands to
requests
via Copilot (yes, I used LLMs to an extent when building this) and started chaining together the requests.
The only issues I faced that took some time to overcome were figuring out how to repeat the requests when needed and being resistant to unexpected HTTP errors. For the former, I initially tried repeating it on an interval (first through a
while True
loop and later via shell scripting in the container) but later realized it was much easier by checking if internet access expired by sending a request to example.com and checking if it fails. For the latter, I used
while True
loops to allow the requests to be retried and executed
break
when the requests succeeded. The only other issue, that still exists, is that occasionally, the connection will drop out while the session is refreshed, although this seems to happen less than every 15 minutes and only lasts for a minute or two.
The container running in Docker Desktop, refreshing the session when needed
After comparing speeds with another guy I met on the cruise (who also happens to be a high-school programmer), who had the highest-level MedallionNet plan, there seems to be no additional throttling (7+ Mbps). Even better, after connecting my power bank’s integrated USB-C cable to the router, I’m able to move around the ship for hours. So far, I’ve been using the router for nearly ~7 hours and my 10,000 mAh power bank is still at 42% battery. In fact, I’m writing this very post while connected to the router.
The script
#
Here’s the code that I’ve been using and a sample .env, although I have a
repository
with the Dockerfile and compose file as well. Also, I’m aware the code isn’t
pretty
, I mostly just wrote it as a proof-of-concept that turned out to work amazingly well. I also doubt I’ll update the code after my cruise ends, since it won’t really be possible to test it. If you try to use this later, and it’s broken, you can go

data.title: If the moon were only 1 pixel: A tediously accurate solar system model (2014)
data.author: sdoering
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要描述了太阳系中各行星之间的巨大距离，强调太空中的 vast 空旷。文章以从地球到火星的旅程为例，说明行星间距离遥远，需要大约七个月的太空旅行才能到达。文章还提到，大多数空间图并未按实际比例绘制，因为太空中的大部分区域都是空旷的。这种空旷超出了人类的直观理解，即使使用比喻或模型也难以准确描述。文章最后反思了人类大脑在处理如此巨大尺度和空无时的局限性，指出我们对宇宙的许多方面难以真正理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“如果月亮只有1像素”的太阳系比例可视化及其相关讨论，包括对宇宙广阔空间的感受、技术实现和类似体验。

不同观点：
• **amelius** 认为光速非常慢，探索其他恒星需要很长时间，可能在拥有全息甲板之前都无法实现。
• **amiga386** 关注HTML/CSS的简单实现，特别是绝对定位和大left值的使用。
• **andersco** 强调这是一种非凡的体验，并提到之前在Hacker News上的讨论。
• **tomxor** 提供了一个192字节的精确太阳系可视化链接，展示了准确的轨道和恒星周期。
• **technothrasher** 分享了小学时使用 vinyl roll 来展示地球历史的类似体验。
• **susam** 提到过去用POV-Ray绘制太阳系行星比例的经验，并讨论了投影方式对视觉效果的影响。
• **robin_reala** 强调光速切换让人感受到宇宙的空旷，等待时间让人深刻理解地球到太阳的距离。
• **jethkl** 提到现实中的太阳系比例模型，并推荐了一些可以步行或骑行的地点。
• **computator** 通过计算说明行星在如此大的比例下仍然可见的奇妙之处。
• **CapsAdmin** 表示尽管看过很多关于宇宙大小的类比，但这次体验尤其震撼，特别是光速的缓慢感。
• **j_m_b** 推荐了Stephen Hawking的Genius中的太阳系比例可视化，并称赞了整个系列。
• **kennu** 抱怨用鼠标滚轮滚动几十万公里太费力，最终放弃了。
• **Symmetry** 指出水星只有1像素大小，并提供了一个照片大小比较的链接。
• **gary17the** 开玩笑说，面对如此广阔的宇宙，如何看待30年还清房贷的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到光速和等待时间，这是体验中的一个重要感受点。
• 不同的技术实现和可视化方法被分享，包括HTML/CSS、POV-Ray和192字节的Dwitter可视化。
• 现实中的太阳系比例模型也被提及，提供了实际的参考。
• 评论中包含了一些关于宇宙广阔和人类渺小的哲学性思考和幽默。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于体验的实际操作性和感受，例如kennu对滚动操作的抱怨，以及amelius对光速缓慢的感慨。

That was about 10 million km (6,213,710 mi) just now.
Pretty empty out here.
Here comes our first planet...
As it turns out, things are pretty far apart.
We’ll be coming up on a new planet soon. Sit tight.
Most of space is just space.
Halfway home.
Destination: Mars!
It would take about seven months to travel this distance in a spaceship.
Better be some good in-flight entertainment.
In case you're wondering, you'd need about 2000 feature-length movies to occupy that many waking hours.
Sit back and relax. Jupiter is more than 3 times as far as we just traveled.
When are we gonna be there?
Seriously. When are we gonna be there?
This is where we might at least see some asteroids to wake us up.
Too bad they're all too small to appear on this map.
I spy, with my little eye... something black.
If you were on a road trip, driving at 75mi/hr, it would have taken you over 500 years to get here from earth.
All these distances are just averages, mind you.
The distance between planets really depends on where the two planets are in their orbits around the sun.
So if you're planning on taking a trip to Jupiter, you might want to use a different map.
If you plan it right, you can actually move relatively quickly between planets.
The New Horizons space craft that launched in 2006 only took 13 months to get to Jupiter.
Don't worry. It'll take a lot less than 13 months to scroll there.
Pretty close to Jupiter now.
Sorry. That was a lie before. Now we really are pretty close.
Lots of time to think out here...
Pop the champagne! We just passed 1 billion km.
I guess this is why most maps of the solar system aren't drawn to scale.
It's not hard to draw the planets.
It's the empty space that's a problem.
Most space charts leave out the most significant part – all the space.
We're used to dealing with things at a much smaller scale than this.
When it comes to things like the age of the earth, the number of snowflakes in Siberia, the national debt...
Those things are too much for our brains to handle.
We need to reduce things down to something we can see or experience directly in order to understand them.
We're always trying to come up with metaphors for big numbers. Even so, they never seem to work.
Let's try a few metaphors anyway...
You would need
of these screens lined up side-by-side to show this whole map at once.
If this map was printed from a quality printer (300 pixels per inch) the earth would be invisible, and the width of the paper would need to be 475 feet.
475 feet is about 1 and 1/2 football fields.
Even though we don’t really understand them, a lot can happen within these massive lengths of time and space.
A drop of water can carve out a canyon.
An amoeba can become a dolphin.
A star can collapse on itself.
It’s easy to disregard nothingness because there’s no thought available to encapsulate it. There’s no metaphor that fits because, by definition, once the nothingness becomes tangible, it ceases to exist.
It’s a good thing we have these tiny stars and planets, otherwise we’d have no point of reference at all.
We’d be surrounded by this stuff that our minds weren’t built to understand.
All this emptiness really could drive you nuts. For instance, if you’re in a sensory deprivation tank for too long, your brain starts to make things up. You see and hear things that aren’t there.
The brain isn't built to handle "empty."
"Sorry, Humanity," says Evolution. "What with all the jaguars trying to eat you, the parasites in your fur, and the never-ending need for a decent steak, I was a little busy. I didn’t exactly have time to come up with a way to conceive of vast stretches of nothingness."
Neurologically speaking, we really only deal with matter of a certain size, and energy of a few select wavelengths. For everything else, we have to make up mental models and see if they match up to the tiny shreds of hard evidence that actually feel real.
The mental models provided by mathematics are extremely helpful when trying to make sense of these vast distances, but still...
Abstraction is pretty unsatisfying.
When you hear people talk about how, "there’s more to this universe than our minds can conceive of" it's usually a way to get you to go along with a half-baked plot point about UFOs or super-powers in a sci-fi series that you're watching late at night when you can’t get to sleep.
Even when Shakespeare wrote: "There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, Than are dreamt of in your philosophy” – he's basically trying to give us a loophole to make the ghost in the story more believable.
But all this empty space, these things of a massive scale, really are more than our minds can conceive of. The maps and metaphors fail to do them justice.
You look at one tiny dot, then you look for the next tiny dot. Everything in between is inconsequential and fairly boring.
Emptiness is actually ever

• **jethkl** 提到现实中的太阳系比例模型，并推荐了一些可以步行或骑行的地点。
• **computator** 通过计算说明行星在如此大的比例下仍然可见的奇妙之处。
• **CapsAdmin** 表示尽管看过很多关于宇宙大小的类比，但这次体验尤其震撼，特别是光速的缓慢感。
• **j_m_b** 推荐了Stephen Hawking的Genius中的太阳系比例可视化，并称赞了整个系列。
• **kennu** 抱怨用鼠标滚轮滚动几十万公里太费力，最终放弃了。
• **Symmetry** 指出水星只有1像素大小，并提供了一个照片大小比较的链接。
• **gary17the** 开玩笑说，面对如此广阔的宇宙，如何看待30年还清房贷的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到光速和等待时间，这是体验中的一个重要感受点。
• 不同的技术实现和可视化方法被分享，包括HTML/CSS、POV-Ray和192字节的Dwitter可视化。
• 现实中的太阳系比例模型也被提及，提供了实际的参考。
• 评论中包含了一些关于宇宙广阔和人类渺小的哲学性思考和幽默。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于体验的实际操作性和感受，例如kennu对滚动操作的抱怨，以及amelius对光速缓慢的感慨。

data.title: How to Build Conscious Machines
data.author: hardmaru
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意识的本质及其在构建有意识机器中的作用

不同观点：
• **canadiantim** 认为，意识的核心问题是“ qualia”（如红色的视觉或咖啡的气味）是否是现实的基本组成部分，还是可以进一步分解为更基础的东西。他批评文章在没有提供证据的情况下，假设qualia可以被分解，并认为文章没有真正触及意识作为真实现象的本质，而只是将其视为一种抽象层。
• **talkingtab** 对文章的方法表示怀疑，认为文章没有回答如何实际构建有意识机器的具体问题。他强调了“知道某事”和“能够做某事”之间的区别，并提出复杂自适应系统（如人类）的例子，认为应从这些系统的构造中寻找线索。
• **esafak** 简要介绍了文章中提出的意识层次结构模型，并关注如何评估有机体所属的意识阶段，同时提到IIT（整合信息理论）作为一种可能的方法。他感兴趣的是如何确定有机体在层次结构中的位置和程度。
• **AIorNot** 质疑任何物理理论是否能够解释意识的本质，指出我们只能通过自己的主观体验来描述意识。他认为文章可能只是讨论了产生意识的条件，而不是解释意识本身。
• **disambiguation** 质疑文章中关于“基质独立性”的假设，认为文章没有充分解释或证明这一点，并将此视为理论的弱点。他还将文章的立场与Penrose的量子二元论进行了比较，认为后者提供了更强的因果机制解释。
• **gcanyon** 提出，意识是否是AI的必要目标值得讨论。他认为，意识可能是高智能系统的副产品，但不一定是目标，目标应是完成具体任务，而非刻意追求意识。
• **Barrin92** 对文章的学术价值表示怀疑，认为其内容像是拼凑而成，缺乏实质性贡献，甚至像是一种恶作剧。
• **PunchTornado** 认为文章中的观点并无新意，很多内容已经在Chalmers和Dennett等人的工作中被更深入地讨论过，批评文章像是半抄袭他人的想法。
• **catigula** 认为，任何声称对意识有完全解释的理论都是误导，推荐了泛心论和Russellian monism作为值得关注的理论。他批评IIT和幻觉主义理论与科学方法不符。
• **kypro** 持有一种极端的观点，认为意识只是大脑为了提升感官重要性而产生的“谎言”，并认为如果有机器能够报告其“痛苦”，那么这种意识与人类的意识并无实质性区别。
• **m3kw9** 质疑如何定义和测试意识，这是一个关键的争议点。
• **briian** 提出，如果对大脑有更好的理解，是否能够更好地模仿意识，并认为这是解锁LLMs（大型语言模型）更多潜力的关键。

补充讨论：
• 意识是否是构建智能机器的必要条件或副产品是一个重要的讨论点，涉及到对意识本质和实用性的不同看法。
• 关于文章中提出的意识层次结构模型，讨论集中在如何评估和验证有机体在层次结构中的位置，以及是否存在更有效的评估方法如IIT。
• 基质独立性和物理理论在解释意识方面的局限性也是一个重要的争议点，特别是与Penrose的量子二元论的比较。
• 对文章的学术价值和原创性的质疑反映了学术界对跨学科理论构建的严格要求。

总结：讨论围绕意识的本质、其在AI中的作用以及如何实际构建有意识机器展开，涉及到哲学、神经科学和计算机科学的多学科交叉观点。

44293260.article_content:
#
Chawan 0.2.0
Version 0.2.0 of the Chawan TUI browser has been released.
A tarball of the source tree is available
here
.  Please refer to the README
file for compilation instructions.
A static binary distribution for
amd64 Linux
also exists.
To install it, extract the archive somewhere and run
make install
as root.  (To uninstall, run
make uninstall
.)
The same distribution is also available as a
.deb
package
.
##
Information for package maintainers
The current list of mandatory runtime dependencies is:
libssh2.
libbrotli (more precisely, libbrotlicommon and libbrotlidec).
OpenSSL or LibreSSL.  For OpenSSL, you will want 3.0 or later.
For LibreSSL, the version in OpenBSD 7.7 has been tested.
Previous development versions had other dependencies which no
longer apply, and can be dropped.  In particular, zlib, libseccomp,
termcap/ncurses and libcurl are no longer used.
If you run into an issue while packaging Chawan, please contact me
before trying to patch over it.  Chances are we can solve it upstream.
##
What's next
It took a bit longer than expected, but I finally feel OK putting a
version on this.  It has all features I wanted from an MVP, and no known
fatal bugs.
The v0.2 branch in git will only receive bugfixes.  Further work on new
features will continue on the master branch.
For the next release, I hope to improve upon the layout module's
performance & correctness, and to make the UI somewhat more user
friendly.  Stay tuned :)

data.title: Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，突破了传统Transformer因自注意力机制带来的二次元内存和计算开销限制。该模型结合了状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多尺度卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，实现了近似线性的计算扩展，适用于处理大规模序列数据。该研究为长文本处理提供了一种新的解决方案，显著提升了处理效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇关于DeepSeek LLM论文的评价与讨论，涉及其架构、实验设计以及是否解决了自注意力机制的二次复杂度问题。

不同观点：
• [albertzeyer] 认为论文中提到的百万到千万级别的token数量与当前的商业LLM在一个数量级，且如果序列长度不比模型维度大很多，自注意力的二次复杂度并不是大问题。他还指出，关于避免二次复杂度的研究已经有很多，但该论文缺乏实验支持，尤其是缺少对长度外推、大规模实验等关键方面的研究。此外，表2中的改进看起来很微小，论文需要更多工作。

• [maxrmk] 对论文中将DeepSeek LLM架构描述得像仍在探索中的观点表示反对，指出DeepSeek的架构已经被充分记录，且有多个实现可以在网上找到。

• [yorwba] 认为论文结构不清晰，重复解释架构但遗漏了关键细节，如“外部检索内存”的梯度计算方法。他还指出，关于DeepSeek LLM的描述过于神秘，尽管已有相关论文发表，无需猜测其是否涉及注意力机制。

• [daxfohl] 提出一个相关问题，即按token收费的商业模式是否可持续。如果计算需求呈二次增长，成本是否也会相应增加？

• [imranq] 对去除二次复杂度的想法表示赞赏，但认为论文的实验支持不足，仅测试了困惑度，缺乏对推理、检索QA或总结质量的测试。尽管如此，他认为去除注意力的模型值得关注。

• [gsf_emergency] 提供了一个非注意力LLM的GitHub链接，作为相关资源。

• [zoklet-enjoyer] 表示对技术细节不了解，但对未来可能性感到兴奋。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是论文的实验设计不足，尤其是缺乏对长度外推等关键问题的研究。
• 另一个争议点是对DeepSeek LLM架构的描述是否清晰、准确。
• 关于按token收费的商业模式在面对计算需求二次增长时的可持续性问题也被提出。
• 尽管论文在实验支持上不足，但部分讨论者对其提出的去除二次复杂度的概念表示出兴趣和期待。

Title:
Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons
Authors:
Andrew Kiruluta
,
Preethi Raju
,
Priscilla Burity
View a PDF of the paper titled Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons, by Andrew Kiruluta and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a novel non attention based architecture for large language models (LLMs) that efficiently handles very long context windows, on the order of hundreds of thousands to potentially millions of tokens. Unlike traditional Transformer designs, which suffer from quadratic memory and computation overload due to the nature of the self attention mechanism, our model avoids token to token attention entirely. Instead, it combines the following complementary components: State Space blocks (inspired by S4) that learn continuous time convolution kernels and scale near linearly with sequence length, Multi Resolution Convolution layers that capture local context at different dilation levels, a lightweight Recurrent Supervisor to maintain a global hidden state across sequential chunks, and Retrieval Augmented External Memory that stores and retrieves high-level chunk embeddings without reintroducing quadratic operations.

44292601.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，突破了传统Transformer因自注意力机制带来的二次元内存和计算开销限制。该模型结合了状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多尺度卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，实现了近似线性的计算扩展，适用于处理大规模序列数据。该研究为长文本处理提供了一种新的解决方案，显著提升了处理效率。
44292601.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇关于DeepSeek LLM论文的评价与讨论，涉及其架构、实验设计以及是否解决了自注意力机制的二次复杂度问题。

不同观点：
• [albertzeyer] 认为论文中提到的百万到千万级别的token数量与当前的商业LLM在一个数量级，且如果序列长度不比模型维度大很多，自注意力的二次复杂度并不是大问题。他还指出，关于避免二次复杂度的研究已经有很多，但该论文缺乏实验支持，尤其是缺少对长度外推、大规模实验等关键方面的研究。此外，表2中的改进看起来很微小，论文需要更多工作。

• [maxrmk] 对论文中将DeepSeek LLM架构描述得像仍在探索中的观点表示反对，指出DeepSeek的架构已经被充分记录，且有多个实现可以在网上找到。

• [yorwba] 认为论文结构不清晰，重复解释架构但遗漏了关键细节，如“外部检索内存”的梯度计算方法。他还指出，关于DeepSeek LLM的描述过于神秘，尽管已有相关论文发表，无需猜测其是否涉及注意力机制。

• [daxfohl] 提出一个相关问题，即按token收费的商业模式是否可持续。如果计算需求呈二次增长，成本是否也会相应增加？

• [imranq] 对去除二次复杂度的想法表示赞赏，但认为论文的实验支持不足，仅测试了困惑度，缺乏对推理、检索QA或总结质量的测试。尽管如此，他认为去除注意力的模型值得关注。

• [gsf_emergency] 提供了一个非注意力LLM的GitHub链接，作为相关资源。

• [zoklet-enjoyer] 表示对技术细节不了解，但对未来可能性感到兴奋。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是论文的实验设计不足，尤其是缺乏对长度外推等关键问题的研究。
• 另一个争议点是对DeepSeek LLM架构的描述是否清晰、准确。
• 关于按token收费的商业模式在面对计算需求二次增长时的可持续性问题也被提出。
• 尽管论文在实验支持上不足，但部分讨论者对其提出的去除二次复杂度的概念表示出兴趣和期待。

data.title: Snorting the AGI with Claude Code
data.author: beigebrucewayne
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（大型语言模型）生成内容及其在软件开发中应用的讨论

不同观点：
• mjrbrennan认为AI生成的总结质量低下，充满空话，不如直接查看代码提交记录来得快而准确，对AI总结的信任度较低。
• blahgeek指出，要求AI解释Rust的借用检查器是一个不好的例子，因为这类数据在AI的训练数据中已经很多，无法展示其真正的能力。
• rbren偏向于围绕LLM无关的开源代理进行脚本编写，认为这项技术正在从根本上改变软件开发，需确保对工作方式的控制。
• jasonthorsness认为终端是LLM的理想接口，可能比自定义IDE集成更受欢迎。
• b0a04gl担心由模型生成描述、测试和样板代码会悄然降低团队的审查标准，建议追踪模型生成代码对长期bug率和回滚模式的影响。
• AstroBen和distortionfield关注的是评论的可读性和博客主题的美观，而非技术内容本身。
• bionhoward对Anthropic的法律条款表示质疑，认为其不合理的条款可能影响其作为AI安全管理者的可信度。
• jvanderbot期待与AI相关的财务投资减少，似乎对AI在软件开发中的角色持保留态度。
• SamPatt和dweinus认为Claude代码的功能强大，特别是在脚本编写方面，能够处理多种任务，但对其价格和准确性存在一定质疑。
• abhisheksp1993对命令行玩笑表示幽默。
• dirtbag__dad对LLM自动化生成变更日志和测试等功能表示赞赏，并询问是否已有类似GitHub actions或pre-commit的工具。
• tinyhouse认为文章内容杂乱，对幻灯片描述代码库的实用性表示怀疑，并指出文中的许多功能并非新颖，且与AGI无关。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对AI生成内容的质量和可信度存在争议，部分人认为不如人工处理可靠。
• LLM在软件开发中的角色和未来应用场景是讨论的焦点，包括其对工作流程的潜在影响和自动化能力的价值。
• 对AI生成内容的长期影响和相关工具的现有实现也有一定讨论。
• 部分评论偏离主题，关注文章的可读性和视觉设计等非技术问题。

data.article_summary: Blaze, a YCombinator-backed startup in Mexico City, is hiring a Junior Software Engineer to help build a cross-border payments app using AI tools. The role involves using AI-driven development tools like Cursor and React to design and implement features for both frontend and backend systems. The successful candidate will collaborate on secure, scalable code for a high-reliability financial app, engage in system design discussions, and stay updated on AI advancements to optimize development practices. Qualifications include experience with AI tools, strong problem-solving skills, proficiency in JavaScript and related technologies, and a passion for fintech. The position offers competitive compensation (MX$200,000/year), equity, mentorship, and a dynamic work environment. Interested candidates should submit a resume, portfolio, and cover letter.

data.title: Retrobootstrapping Rust for some reason
data.author: romac
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到用户被随机选中进行CAPTCHA验证以确认请求有效。页面提供了一个登录表单，包括账户名、密码输入框和“记住我”选项。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的选项。用户需完成CAPTCHA验证才能继续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： reproducing old builds of LLVM and Rust, and the challenges associated with backwards compatibility and bootstrapping in modern compilers.

不同观点：
• **Kimixa** 认为，现代的 clang 和 gcc 无法编译旧版本的 LLVM，主要是由于 C++ 标准的变化。通过在编译选项中指定 "std=xxx" 可以解决此问题。他还提到，自己成功编译了2011年左右的LLVM版本，但遇到了一些LLVM代码中的bug。Kimixa 还指出，C++ 对旧代码的兼容性支持过于僵化，对新版本的发展有负面影响。

• **Jasonthorsness** 对即使在2011年这么近的时间点上重现构建也存在困难感到担忧，并质疑技术是否会稳定下来，还是会变得更糟。他提出了一个更广泛的问题：将来是否会遇到现有技术无法再构建的情况。

• **LegionMammal978** 分享了自己在Ubuntu 20.04上进行类似项目的经验，遇到了LLVM堆栈问题，并且一些提交的哈希在公共repo中找不到。这增加了重建缺失提交的工作量。

• **Tmtvl** 提到Guix在引导Rust时遇到了问题，并引用了一篇2018年的文章。这表明Rust的 bootstrapping 问题在不同的项目中都有出现。

• **Neilv** 提出是否可以创建一个简化的Rust编译器实现，接受最新的Rust语言输入但不做检查，仅用于最小化步骤的可持续引导。他还赞扬了Debian在维护旧软件包方面的成功。

补充讨论：
• **Gregorvand** 和 **fcoury** 提到了访问某些链接时遇到的问题，并提供了替代链接以帮助访问被禁止的内容。

• **Eptcyka** 对Nix evangelists的某些行为提出批评，但承认在重现构建问题时，使用Nix固定nixpkgs版本和源代码可以减轻负担。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于C++和Rust等语言对旧代码的兼容性支持是否合理，以及这种支持是否对语言的现代发展造成了不必要的负担。Kimixa认为这种兼容性过度僵化，而Neilv则在寻找一种简化的编译器实现来解决引导问题。

• socalgal2遇到了实际使用中的问题，具体是找不到“Add”按钮，影响了其使用体验。

• WhitneyLand指出了一个UX问题：在进行捏拉缩放（pinch zoom）操作时界面出现异常行为，建议要么支持双指手势，要么禁用该功能以避免干扰。

• kube-system对该工具的实际应用场景表示好奇，询问了其可能的用例。

• guigui提到在白色背景上，控制按钮看起来像是被禁用的，这可能是UI设计上的一个问题。

• Eduard在Android的Chrome浏览器上遇到了两指输入的问题，导致已放置的对象出现跳动和消失的现象。

• hoppp以一种幽默的方式表达了对工具功能的探索，但并未提出具体建议或问题。

• echelon对工具的创意潜力表示认可，特别是2D界面操控3D对象的功能，但建议去掉与加密相关的内容，以更专注于创意画布的扩展。

补充讨论：
• 关于R3F的讨论显示出用户对其在3D编辑器开发中的潜力有兴趣，特别是在简化3D操作和提高用户友好性方面。
• 多个用户（WhitneyLand和Eduard）报告了移动端手势操作的问题，表明该工具在移动设备上的UX可能需要改进。
• echelon的评论引发了关于工具未来方向的讨论，特别是在去掉某些内容以专注于创意功能方面的建议。

争议焦点：
• 目前主要的争议集中在移动端手势操作的问题上，用户在使用双指缩放时遇到了界面异常和对象跳动的情况。这表明在跨平台支持和用户体验一致性方面还有改进空间。
